record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: What role does magnetic proximity from the ferromagnetic layer play in the exchange-bias effect observed in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals and related heterostructures?

evidence.quote: viii. What is the role of magnetic proximity of the FM layer on the EB effect in FM/AFM vdW and related systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterostructure consisting of a ferromagnetic (FM) layer placed in atomic contact with an antiferromagnetic (AFM) layer, where at least one of the constituents is a two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic material (for example, FM materials such as Fe3GeTe2 paired with AFM materials such as CrCl3, FePS3, MnPS3, or NiPS3, as well as related layered systems). After field cooling such a bilayer below the Néel temperature of the AFM layer, the hysteresis loop of the FM layer is typically shifted along the magnetic-field axis; this shift is the exchange-bias (EB) effect. Separately, the magnetic proximity effect refers to the modification of magnetic properties (induced magnetization, magnetic transition temperature, coercivity, magnetic anisotropy, and spin texture) of one layer near the interface due to its proximity to the magnetically ordered partner layer.

Problem. Determine, in a quantitative and mechanism-resolved manner, the role played by the magnetic proximity effect originating from the FM layer in producing the exchange-bias effect observed in FM/AFM van der Waals (and related layered) heterostructures. Specifically:

(a) Identify how proximity-induced magnetization, modified anisotropy, and interfacial spin reconstruction in the AFM layer near the FM/AFM interface contribute to the magnitude, sign, and thermal stability of the EB field H_EB and to the enhanced coercivity H_C.

(b) Derive or specify a microscopic model (e.g., an interfacial Heisenberg-type exchange Hamiltonian including proximity-induced moments and uncompensated AFM spins) that separates the proximity contribution from other interfacial mechanisms (frozen uncompensated spins, domain-wall pinning, spin-flop coupling), and predict H_EB as a function of AFM thickness, FM thickness, temperature, and field-cooling protocol.

(c) Propose experimentally testable signatures that isolate the proximity contribution to EB in such van der Waals heterostructures.
artifact.category_tag: Exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2024) on van der Waals FM/AFM heterostructures such as Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3, Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, and CrI3-based junctions reports exchange-bias and proximity phenomena, but the specific role of magnetic proximity from the FM layer in producing EB is still being actively investigated and is identified as an open question in review-level discussions; no consensus mechanism quantitatively isolating the proximity contribution has been established.

status_evidence.title: Emergent Multifunctional Magnetic Proximity in van der Waals Layered Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Magnetic proximity effects can control material functionalities such as magnetic transition temperature, coercivity, magnetic anisotropy, and exchange bias effect.
status_evidence.claim: Magnetic proximity is recognized to influence EB but the exact mechanism in vdW FM/AFM systems remains under study.

status_evidence.title: Manipulating exchange bias in 2D magnetic heterojunction for high-performance robust memory applications
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange bias effects have recently been reported in a variety of low-dimensional van der Waals magnetic systems.
status_evidence.claim: EB in vdW heterostructures is an active research area without a settled proximity-based theory.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias in van der Waals CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2 Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Reports EB in CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2 and discusses interfacial coupling mechanisms.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental EB observed but proximity role not fully quantified.
